answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly to hold: every wallet must post a bonded stake locked for many epochs, and payment arrives only after peers attest real work. A Sybil operator launching a thousand puppets must fund a thousand stakes and keep them locked through each checkpoint, so cost scales with fake identities while income does not. Fresh keys start at zero reputation, so answers split apart as by a prism. Each vote passes through a narrow inlet of verified history, and a ripple of copied work spreads no further than the stake behind it.
